nodes.label: NOTE: The localhost→127.0.0.1 redirect was removed. It split the browser
nodes.norm_label: note: the localhost→127.0.0.1 redirect was removed. it split the browser

nodes.label: Recurring Payment Plan Model (Mobile)
nodes.rationale: Schedule-locked chains (due slot = plan_start_date + N x cycle; late pays never shift the plan); billing mode pay_on_due shows a due card + explicit Mark Paid (never silent money) vs auto_charge posted by the generator; shared idempotent payment surface (markOccurrencePaid / skip / undo / payPlanFromForm with chain re-anchor).

nodes.label: public.bank_accounts Table
nodes.rationale: current_balance column is not authoritative — live balances are computed client-side from expenses + transfers + initial; one default per user via partial unique index.

nodes.label: public.bin_receipt_orphans Table
nodes.rationale: Nightly purge (pg_cron spendflow-bin-purge 03:30 UTC) queues expired binned expenses' receipt paths here via SECURITY DEFINER functions (zero RLS policies); the owner's next Bin visit drains them client-side via claim_bin_receipt_orphans().

nodes.label: public.categories Table
nodes.rationale: expenses/recurring_rules category_id FKs are ON DELETE RESTRICT — clients must reassign to a fallback category before deleting (mobile does).

nodes.label: public.expenses Table
nodes.rationale: Central ledger row: CHECK date 2000-01-01..today+1, FX snapshot columns, receipt path, soft delete, and UNIQUE (recurring_rule_id, recurring_due_date) dedup; client_sync_id kept as a future offline-queue hook with its unique index intentionally dropped.

nodes.label: Per-Row FX Snapshot Columns
nodes.rationale: exchange_rate_to_usd + base_currency stamped at creation so historical views use each row's own-date rate, not today's — analytics/pivot logic depends on snapshots and the web must reproduce them or numbers diverge from mobile.

nodes.label: public.notifications Table
nodes.rationale: Client-inserted on budget milestones (parity behavior on web); became the dedup source of truth for milestone alerts after the localStorage purge bug fix (2026-09-15).

nodes.label: public.recurring_rules Table
nodes.rationale: 20260915 plan model: frequency incl. custom interval_days 1-365, mode pay_on_due/auto_charge, plan_start_date chain anchor, deleted_at Bin flag; WARNING bank_account_id exists in migration but was never applied live — never write it.

nodes.label: public.transfers Table
nodes.rationale: FX rate locked on the row at creation: CHECK |converted_amount - amount x exchange_rate| <= 0.05 and from_account <> to_account; insert-only with no update path.

nodes.label: P2-5: Recurring-Slot Squatting
nodes.rationale: createExpense stamped recurring_rule_id/due_date from caller input with no ownership check — an attacker's row legitimately occupying a slot swallows the victim's idempotent upsert so their installment never books; RLS structurally cannot catch it; mitigated client-side, trigger question raised for the mobile repo.

nodes.label: receipts Storage Bucket (private)
nodes.rationale: 4 MiB image allowlist, owner-folder paths {uid}/..., reads via 1-hour signed URLs (download-disposition variant post-audit so no object renders top-level), INSERT blocked while deletion_pending.

nodes.label: SCHEMA.md — SpendFlow Database Schema
nodes.rationale: Derived from reading all 34 committed SQL migrations in order (Supabase CLI not installed); this column-level contract is what web code must match until supabase gen types replaces/augments it.

nodes.label: Recurring Slot-Key Dedup Index
nodes.rationale: UNIQUE (recurring_rule_id, recurring_due_date) is non-partial: payment dates vary with late pays but slots don't, so a soft-deleted occurrence still holds its slot and 'Not paid — undo' must HARD-delete to free it; the old (recurring_rule_id, date) index is gone live — any upsert on it errors 42P10.

nodes.label: Soft Delete / 60-day Bin Pattern
nodes.rationale: deleted_at = now() makes expense and recurring-plan deletion a restorable Bin state (60 days); the web must never hard-delete either row outside services/bin.ts; queries filter deleted_at IS NULL exactly like mobile so stale clients can't resurrect rows.

nodes.label: No Offline Mutation Queue
nodes.rationale: The queue was removed from mobile and client_sync_id's unique index deliberately dropped; all writes online-only on both clients, and web must NOT add one — it would break parity; concurrent edits are last-write-wins per whole-row UPDATE.

nodes.label: External Public HTTP APIs (FX, Gold, Push)
nodes.norm_label: external public http apis (fx, gold, push)
nodes.rationale: Unauthenticated public endpoints (open.er-api.com, api.frankfurter.app, api.gold-api.com, exp.host); nothing sensitive is sent; a CORS or rate-limit problem is solved by a new/extended edge function, never a Next.js proxy holding keys.

nodes.label: @supabase/ssr Cookie Session Handling
nodes.rationale: Cookie-based session storage (not localStorage) so Server Components and middleware can read the session; middleware verifies the JWT server-side per request with auth.getUser(), failing closed — the web equivalent of mobile's SecureStore adapter.

nodes.label: public.exchange_rates Table
nodes.rationale: Shared reference data PK (currency, date); clients are read-only, writes are service-role/backfill; QAR/AED/SAR pegged (never stored/fetched), NPR = INR/1.6 derived.

nodes.label: P2-1: Missing CSP (Doc Claimed It Existed)
nodes.norm_label: p2-1: missing csp (doc claimed it existed)
nodes.rationale: next.config.ts shipped every header SECURITY.md claimed except CSP — a doc-vs-code drift finding; remediated by shipping the documented non-nonce CSP with HSTS and pinned connect-src/img-src hosts.

nodes.label: P2-4: Missing Owner-Scope on Mutations
nodes.rationale: Defense-in-depth inversion: services omitted the .eq('user_id', …) predicates their docs called defense in depth, so a single future policy relaxation becomes cross-tenant; fixed by making userId params required everywhere (services/bin.ts was the correct template).

nodes.label: P2-6: Reset/Signup Redirects Off-Allowlist
nodes.rationale: Non-/auth/callback redirect targets were silently rewritten to the spendflow:// Site URL (dead web recovery flows); fixed to bare /auth/callback with live probe verification and type=recovery landing on /profile?recovery=1.

nodes.label: P3-9: Enumeration-Safe Auth Messaging
nodes.rationale: Sign-in maps wrong-email and wrong-password to one generic message; the reset flow's existence-answering posture was later changed by owner request (2026-09-15) with a DB-backed cooldown as the mitigation.

nodes.label: send-password-reset Flow (2026-09-15)
nodes.rationale: Brokered by an edge function that answers account existence (owner-requested, replacing the former P3-9 neutral posture) but stamps a DB-backed 60 s per-email cooldown for FOUND and NOT-FOUND alike, so existence-probing is rate-limited as hard as mail spamming; links target the bare allowlisted /auth/callback.

nodes.label: API.md — Web-facing API Surface
nodes.rationale: The web app is a direct Supabase client (like mobile) with no BFF layer in v1; the doc covers browser-called edge functions, external HTTP APIs, and a deliberately minimal Next.js server surface.

nodes.label: Full Security Audit 2026-09-14 (v2 Consolidated)
nodes.rationale: Read-only line-by-line re-audit: verdict — no critical/high exploitable against a correctly-configured backend, but the whole posture rests on the live DB matching the docs (real prior drift); 0 P0 / 0 P1 / 7 P2 / 11 P3 / 5 P4, with all web-side items remediated the same day.

nodes.label: Client-Direct Supabase (No BFF)
nodes.rationale: The web app is a second client of the same backend, not a BFF: all authorization happens through the exact RLS policies the mobile app relies on; the anon key is public by design.

nodes.label: Known Live Migration Drift
nodes.rationale: Migrations are not proof of live state: recurring_rules.bank_account_id never applied; transfers CHECKs had to be re-asserted in migration 34; migration 21's storage limits superseded by 29 — security-critical facts must be verified against the live DB.

nodes.label: Content-Security-Policy Posture (Non-Nonce)
nodes.rationale: Implemented 2026-09-14: connect-src/img-src pinned to the four outbound origins, frame-ancestors none, HSTS; deliberately non-nonce because nonce CSP would force dynamic rendering on every page (static landing, /preview*, CDN), and 'unsafe-inline' is accepted since app code has no HTML sinks — remote-script/egress lockdown carries the defense; it is also the compensating control for ssr session state readable by JS.

nodes.label: OAuth Redirect Allowlist (spendflow:// Rewrite Bug)
nodes.rationale: The project's Site URL is the mobile deep link spendflow://, and Supabase silently rewrites any non-allowlisted redirect_to to it — the 'Google login opens the APK' symptom. Fix is dashboard-only: allowlist each exact origin as <origin>/auth/callback (loopback IPs auto-allowed, localhost hostname is not); never wildcard; verified via scripts/verify-oauth-redirect.mjs.

nodes.label: RLS as the Actual Security Boundary
nodes.norm_label: rls as the actual security boundary
nodes.rationale: The anon key is public by design on both clients, so owner-scoped RLS on all tables, revoked client DELETEs, validate_owned_references() triggers, and zero-policy service-role tables are the real boundary; client-side checks are UX only — never propose weakening a policy to ease a web feature.

nodes.label: Lucide-Only Icon Rule
nodes.rationale: The shared DB stores category/account icons as emoji (mobile writes them); stored glyphs are data, never rendered as text — every UI icon is a lucide-react component resolved through components/ui/Glyph.tsx.

nodes.label: change-email.html Template
nodes.rationale: Sent to the NEW address mid-way through the profile email-change flow, after the OTP on the current address has been verified; uses {{ .Email }} and {{ .NewEmail }}.

nodes.label: confirm-signup.html Template
nodes.rationale: Uses GoTrue-built {{ .ConfirmationURL }} (never hand-assembled auth URLs, since the redirect allowlist is baked into it); link lands on the bare allowlisted /auth/callback.

nodes.label: security-code.html Template (Magic Link slot)
nodes.rationale: HARD RULE: must keep {{ .Code }} — both apps' account-deletion and email-change flows code-type the OTP, so dropping it breaks them silently; live mailer_otp_length=8, expiry 3600 s; the ConfirmationURL link is only a fallback.

nodes.label: send-security-otp Edge Function
nodes.rationale: POST {purpose: account_deletion|email_change}; recipient always resolved server-side from the JWT — the client never supplies an email; 60 s per-user-per-purpose cooldown (429 cooldown_active).

nodes.label: Mobile Canonical Palette (Parchment/Teal, Slate/Indigo)
nodes.rationale: Light = warm parchment #EDEAE0 + teal #0F5C4D; dark = deep slate #0B0F19 + indigo #818CF8 — mirrored from the mobile constants/theme.ts and (per the 2026-09-15 status note) now mirrored token-for-token by app/globals.css.

nodes.label: Theme Token Bridge (CSS Vars)
nodes.rationale: Tailwind CSS variables under :root/.dark map semantic token names (bg-primary, text-text) so components never carry raw hex; class-strategy dark mode toggled by the ThemeContext port — goal: the web app is visually indistinguishable from mobile in both themes; do not 'improve' the palette.

nodes.label: Neo Palette Divergence (Reversed 2026-09-15)
nodes.rationale: The web had diverged to a 'Neo' soft-fintech palette (porcelain #f3f5f3 + emerald #0b8457 light; near-black + mint dark); on 2026-09-15 the user reversed it — globals.css now mirrors constants/theme.ts and the Neo red/mint chart rule is retired.

nodes.label: public.security_otp_sends Table
nodes.rationale: OTP cooldown ledger (composite PK user_id+purpose); RLS on with zero policies and all grants revoked — service-role only, invisible to every client.

nodes.label: emails/README.md — Auth Email Templates
nodes.rationale: Templates live in the Supabase project (Dashboard → Email Templates), not the app — one set serves both clients with no deploy; four templates exist because SpendFlow triggers exactly four auth emails.

nodes.label: Chart Series Color Rule
nodes.rationale: Income series is always the income (green) token; the expense series is theme-conditional via a single expenseColor variable (primary in dark, danger in light) so both clients' charts read identically.

nodes.label: Bullion Market Calibrations (FENEGOSIDA / IBJA)
nodes.rationale: Nepal FENEGOSIDA official fix (10:30 AM NPT; fine gold 1.20649, Tejabi 92.5588%, silver 1.22765) and India IBJA (AM/PM IST fixes; 1.0918 duty+GST calibration, 22K at 91.67%) — must stay byte-identical between clients.

nodes.label: public.market_gold_rates Table
nodes.rationale: FENEGOSIDA daily fix rows (UNIQUE rate_date, country_code) written only by the pg_cron edge function; authenticated SELECT only; the Nepal bullion board must show ONLY verified rows.

nodes.label: public.user_settings_history Table (Append-only)
nodes.rationale: Budget/cycle change trail: baseline row 1900-01-01, UNIQUE (user_id, effective_from), trigger-gated to baseline-or-current-month inserts, DELETE revoked — so past cycles compute with the budget active at the time.

nodes.label: public.users Table
nodes.rationale: Profile row: preferred_currency, theme_preference, monthly_budget stored once with its own budget_currency (display conversion only), cycle_start_day 1 = calendar sentinel (29-31 valid), deletion_pending server-managed; no client DELETE.

nodes.label: P2-2: Live Bucket Limits Unverified
nodes.rationale: Client upload gates are browser-checkable labels; SECURITY.md §8 and the audit doc contradicted on whether migration 21 or 29 limits were live — closed by a REST probe showing exactly the documented limits; web hardened anyway (download-disposition receipt links).

nodes.label: avatars Storage Bucket (public)
nodes.rationale: 2 MiB allowlist, owner-folder writes, public SELECT; being public it drove the canvas-re-encode fix (P2-3) and the stored avatar_url prefix validation (P3-2).

nodes.label: Byte-Compatible Cross-Client Invariants
nodes.rationale: Six shared-dataflow invariants that must match exactly between clients: FX snapshot tier order, budget/cycle math, bullion calibrations, recurring idempotent generation, balance computation, and i18n key names.

nodes.label: Trilingual i18n Coverage Rule
nodes.rationale: Every user-facing string is added to all three i18n files (en, hi, ne) in the same change so both clients' translations stay synchronized.

nodes.label: Avatar EXIF/GPS Canvas Re-encode
nodes.rationale: Phone-camera JPEGs carry GPS/device/timestamp metadata; since avatars land in a public-read bucket, images are canvas re-encoded (<=512 px webp/jpeg) client-side before upload so metadata never reaches it (audit P2-3), and stored avatar_url is validated to the avatars-bucket prefix on write and render (P3-2).

nodes.label: Logic Parity Tests
nodes.rationale: The riskiest web/mobile divergence is pure math (cycle windows, budget conversion, FX tiers, bullion calibrations, minor-unit reconciliation) — port mobile behavior and lock it with unit tests, including the regression guard that stored budgets are never rewritten by display conversion.

nodes.label: supabase/tests/rls_regression.sql (49 pgTAP Assertions)
nodes.rationale: Backend RLS is verified by the mobile repo's pgTAP suite (cross-user isolation, owned-reference rejection, read-only rates, CHECKs); web does not duplicate it but re-runs it after any migration, plus an E2E user-A-cannot-read-user-B smoke.

nodes.label: Completion Bar (Definition of Done)
nodes.rationale: Six items: mobile-parity implementation, tsc 0 errors + clean lint, tests pass, docs updated (FEATURE-PARITY row), no schema/RLS regression, and a ponytail over-engineering sweep on the diff before done.

nodes.label: Ponytail Simplicity Discipline
nodes.rationale: Preventive search-before-build rules plus a final ponytail-review diff sweep; explicitly NOT shortest-code: never remove validation, error handling, security, accessibility, or tests to shrink code, and documented rules win over minimalism.

nodes.label: Mobile Auth & Session Flow (End to End)
nodes.norm_label: mobile auth & session flow (end to end)
nodes.rationale: Chunked SecureStore session adapter, OAuth deep-link trust gate (login-CSRF defense), soft-lock biometrics, ensureProfile bootstrap, OTP-gated email change, and a fail-closed account-deletion state machine requiring a fresh OTP-minted session.

nodes.label: delete-account Edge Function
nodes.rationale: Requires a Bearer token whose amr contains a fresh (<=10 min) otp/magiclink entry; runs a fail-closed wipe state machine (deletion_pending flag, storage purge, delete_user_data RPC, admin.deleteUser last) — never reimplemented client-side.

nodes.label: No Service-Role Key in Web — Ever
nodes.norm_label: no service-role key in web — ever
nodes.rationale: Server-side privileged operations already exist as edge functions (delete-account, send-security-otp) reused as-is; any future server-privilege need becomes an edge function in the mobile repo, never a Next.js route holding the key.

nodes.label: Mobile-First Every Screen Rule
nodes.rationale: Pages are designed at 390 px first then enhanced upward (sm/md/lg), never desktop-first with shrink-to-fit; phones get the full feature set (progressive enhancement, not a stripped view), verified by shot-preview scripts at 4 widths x 2 themes.

nodes.label: fetch-nepal-gold-rate Edge Function
nodes.rationale: Service-role / pg_cron only — the web must never call it.

nodes.label: pg_cron Nepal Gold Rate Schedules
nodes.rationale: 4 schedules (11:00/11:15/11:30/12:00 NPT) POST to fetch-nepal-gold-rate with the service key from vault.decrypted_secrets; first verified fetch of the day wins (idempotent).

nodes.label: Turborepo Monorepo Target Decision
nodes.rationale: One backend, two consumers: shared GENERATED Supabase types catch the exact class of schema-drift bug found in mobile migrations (e.g. recurring_rules.bank_account_id never applied live); shared business logic (currency math, FX snapshots, bullion calibrations, i18n keys) plus one migration folder and one RLS source of truth.

nodes.label: Phase 0 Standalone-Repo Interim
nodes.rationale: The mobile repo is a deployed standalone EAS app; moving it into apps/mobile changes EAS project paths and risks the release pipeline — unacceptable as a bootstrapping side effect, so the restructure is explicitly deferred and types are synced by a script copying into both repos.

nodes.label: bullion-history Edge Function
nodes.rationale: GET ?days=30..400 returning Yahoo futures rows with CORS *; exists because browsers/native cannot hit Yahoo directly — web must use it instead of calling Yahoo itself.

nodes.label: scripts/sync-supabase-types.mjs
nodes.rationale: Phase-0 substitute for a shared packages/types: runs supabase gen types typescript and copies database.types.ts into both repos so neither hand-duplicates types; CI (later) diffs the generated file so drift fails the build.

nodes.label: Graphify Codebase Intelligence Skill
nodes.rationale: Turns the repo into a persistent knowledge graph (graphify-out/) as a navigation aid for cross-file/cross-module work; not a source of truth — the priority-of-information order still governs, and it must not be run for trivial changes.

nodes.label: Mobile-Only Behaviors to Adapt or Skip on Web
nodes.norm_label: mobile-only behaviors to adapt or skip on web
nodes.rationale: Biometric lock, screenshot blocking, haptics, push, on-device OCR, Apple sign-in, and swipe gestures are skipped or mapped to web equivalents (file input, blob downloads, toasts) for web v1.

nodes.label: Shared Supabase Project stisbfahlhquaqhrifjh
nodes.rationale: One Supabase project, two consumers (mobile + web) that must feel like one product; the mobile repo owns supabase/migrations/, and all edge functions deploy with verify_jwt = true.

nodes.label: Width-Locked Privacy Masking
nodes.rationale: Global eye toggle masks money as bullet characters with the container width locked (tabular-nums) so adjacent delta badges never shift when toggling.

nodes.label: Required States Per Screen
nodes.rationale: Every screen implements loading skeletons (never blank, never layout shift), empty with primary action, inline+toast errors with retry, success toasts after mutations, and disabled in-flight submits.

nodes.label: Route-to-Screen Parity Map
nodes.rationale: Web routes map 1:1 to mobile expo-router routes so the two feel like one product; modals-on-mobile become dialogs/drawers or pages on web.

nodes.label: SpendFlow Mobile App (Expo SDK 57)
nodes.rationale: The deployed Expo/RN companion app owning supabase/migrations/, services/, constants/theme.ts and constants/i18n/ — the web app is a second client of its backend and mirrors its behavior.

nodes.label: 00 — Existing App Audit (SpendFlow Mobile)
nodes.rationale: Designated source of truth for the web app: everything was read directly from the mobile repo and its 34 committed SQL migrations (audit date 2026-09-12).

nodes.label: FEATURE-PARITY.md — Mobile vs Web
nodes.rationale: Feature-by-feature status ledger (done/planned/deferred/N-A); deliberate web divergences (e.g. slide-over record sheets, richer History filters, mobile-1:1 rebuilds) are recorded here as scope decisions, never silent rewrites.

nodes.label: Priority of Information Order
nodes.rationale: When sources disagree, explicit user instruction beats the mobile audit, which beats ARCHITECTURE.md, which beats other docs; general assumptions are a last resort and a smell. This ordering exists because guessing at undocumented mobile behavior produces a second product.

nodes.label: Cache-then-Network Sync Model
nodes.rationale: Paint disposable local cache instantly, throttled (30 s) network refresh, in-memory listener sets for cross-screen freshness; Supabase Postgres is the single source of truth and web never fetches more eagerly than mobile.

nodes.label: No-Realtime Decision
nodes.rationale: Realtime would require adding tables to the supabase_realtime publication (a backend change affecting both clients) while mobile doesn't consume it — the apps could still diverge; refresh-on-focus polling matches mobile exactly.
